items.title: Mozambique Chamber of Commerce launches Social Responsibility Award
items.summary: On the occasion, CCM Vice-President for Internal Affairs Ilda Matabel said the award also seeks to raise the profile of initiatives which, despite producing positive results in communities, do not always receive the recognition they deserve “May this award serve as a platform for sharing experiences and bringing the business sector and communities closer together,” Matabel said, stressing that the CCM hopes to support companies that have contributed to improving people’s quality of life, particularly in the most vulnerable communities Photo: Câmara de Comércio de Moçambique The Chairman of the Board of Directors of the Mozambique Chamber of Commerce and Investments (CCMI), Thani Cabir, said that social responsibility should be regarded as an investment in the country’s future, stressing that business growth should go hand in hand with the development of the communities in which companies operate For her part, the Vice-President of the Social Responsibility and Sustainability portfolio at CCM, Felícia Nhama, explained that the initiative is open to small, medium-sized and large…

items.title: French blood banks targeted by refrigerator cyberattack
items.summary: A cyberattack had attempted to destroy blood plasma by raising the temperatures in cold storage facilities past the boiling point Blood banks in France were included among cyberattacks that hit refrigeration systems in several European countries on Sunday and Monday, French authorities said on Wednesday The French Blood Establishment (EFS) said that a " cybersecurity incident "targeted a refrigeration service provider affecting control systems at three cold storage sites for plasma and blood samples The cyberattack attempted to raise temperatures to extremely high levels but it was warded off before any damage could be done.

items.title: Africa's shifting role in the global drug trade
items.summary: Recent discoveries of meth labs suggest parts of Africa are moving beyond drug transit and becoming sites of synthetic drug production For years, Africa was primarily known as a transit point for international drug trafficking networks But recent drug seizures and laboratory discoveries show that illicit drugs are no longer only passing through African countries — they are increasingly being manufactured there Recent discoveries of methamphetamine laboratories in countries such as Nigeria , South Africa , Kenya and Mozambique have fueled concerns that Africa is becoming a significant production hub for synthetic drugs According to the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), synthetic drug production increasingly involves transnational criminal networks and clandestine laboratories capable of supplying both local and international markets The debate gained new urgency this year after Nigeria's National Drug Law Enforcement Agency (NDLEA) dismantled what the agency described as the largest clandestine methamphetamine laboratory ever uncovered in the country The operation in Nigeria's…

items.title: Wawira Njirum, Kenya's school feeder and German Africa Prize recipient
items.summary: From a small fundraiser to a major enterprise, Wawira Njiru's Kenyan school feeding scheme has been more successful than she ever thought possible. She's now being awarded the German Africa Prize From starting a modest fundraiser for 25 school children, Wawira Njiru, 35, has become a social entrepreneur with a staggering 6,000 staff on her payroll, feeding 600,000 kids in Kenya every day with her organization Food4Education (F4E), an engagement for which she is being honored with this year's German Africa Prize . How did this transformation come to pass? The answer may be in her character. Stubborn and hardworking, that's how Njiru sees herself. "It's hard to tell me something is not possible." Thinking back to how she began, she explained, "My dream then, my ambition was to feed 100 kids every day.

items.title: US midterm results a 'victory' for Canadians hopeful of tariff relief
items.summary: US tariffs on Canada featured heavily in Michigan and Maine, where Democratic candidates won big on Tuesday It was the midterm result that many in Canada had hoped for - a Democratic sweep that was in part a repudiation by American voters of Donald Trump's tariff on close trade allies "I was doing cartwheels down the street," said Ontario Premier Doug Ford on Wednesday morning, calling it "a victory for Canada" Tuesday night's result is unlikely to grant Canada relief from those tariffs any time soon, but there is anticipation that the political shifts could create a more favourable environment for Ottawa to get the best deal now that on-again-off-again trade talks are back on US voters cited affordability as a main concern heading into the midterms and a survey by the Cato Institute in September , external suggested that about 75% believe the tariffs have raised prices In states like Maine and Michigan, tariffs played a significant role in the hard-fought races In Maine, incumbent Republican Senator Susan Collins clashed with the White House over tariffs She successfully lobbied to…

items.title: Iran's chief negotiator says Americans voted 'no to war'
items.summary: Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf said Iran "endorsed" the message sent by American voters Iran's chief negotiator in talks with the US has said that Americans voted "NO TO WAR", after President Donald Trump's Republican Party suffered a stunning defeat in the midterm elections "We endorse this message," parliament speaker Mohammed Bagher Ghalibaf wrote on X "If the US [government] betrays their public will to serve international paymasters and blackmailers, it will learn our NO comes with a Nightmare," he warned Trump acknowledged on Tuesday that the poor results for Republican congressional candidates were partly due to the war and the related surge in petrol prices.

items.title: ANC under pressure to reverse South Africa decline
items.summary: More than 500 parties are contesting the elections South Africans are voting in highly contested local elections likely to see a haemorrhaging of votes for the country's biggest party, the African National Congress (ANC) This year's voting season has been marked by intense campaigns that have included politicians spinning cars, watching grannies knit and even wading through giant-sized potholes Election officials say voting is going smoothly, despite long queues at some polling stations Leaders are campaigning to head South Africa's nearly 300 municipalities, responsible for basic service provision such as water, electricity and refuse collection For the ANC, the elections are a chance to prove it still has what it takes to govern.

items.title: UK national tests positive for Ebola virus in DR Congo
items.summary: DR Congo has been facing the deadliest Ebola outbreak in the country's history A British national who is in the Democratic Republic of Congo has tested positive for Ebola, the UK government has confirmed A spokesperson said the UK "has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this" and that the risk to the public remains low It is the first confirmed case of a UK national contracting Ebola during the most recent outbreak of the rare but deadly virus in DR Congo, which has so far led to more than 5,000 deaths The Foreign Office did not confirm whether the patient would be brought back to the UK for treatment, though a UK resident who was exposed to the virus in July was flown back for medical attention, as have previous nationals infected abroad Reuters news agency reported the most recent patient is a healthcare worker and would be brought to the UK, citing an internal document BBC News has not seen A UK government spokesperson said: "The UK has well-established procedures for dealing with cases like this, and those processes have been activated "Further information…
